text: Picking a side would have been the wrong move. Both of Lesson 23's positions were legitimate, so Mara proposes a phased compromise instead: identity and segmentation ship during the outage window, in shadow mode, logging every decision without blocking anything yet.

A 14-day validation gate follows the window. The dual-check methodology reconciles every logged access decision against group membership and direct grants — the same check that caught the original gap, now run before enforcement instead of after.

Three measurable pass criteria decide it: zero unplanned operational interruptions, one hundred percent of logged access accounted for, and any discrepancy resolved before the gate closes. If one fails, enforcement waits and the failure says exactly what to fix.

This isn't a new idea — it's the same principle the capstone has used since Lesson 12: don't trust a single check, and don't call something validated until independent evidence says so. Next lesson runs that same discipline across the whole program.
